Corticospinal tract degeneration defines this pure spastic paraplegia; weakness and amyotrophy reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than primary myopathy.
Immune-mediated necrotizing scleritis causes scleral thinning and destruction; associated systemic autoimmune diseases are separate conditions.
Glycolytic enzyme deficiency causes hemolytic anemia; myopathy/rhabdomyolysis and neurodevelopmental dysfunction each occur in 30-79%; renal and retinal disease are under 30%.
Benign tumor of the pharynx, which belongs to the pulmonary axis under the specified mapping.
HTLV-1-associated mature T-cell leukemia/lymphoma; direct cutaneous infiltration occurs in roughly 30-50%, varying by clinical subtype.
Polydactyly establishes skeletal involvement; no definition or phenotype evidence supports additional organs or assuming the full Apert syndrome phenotype.
A medial longitudinal fasciculus lesion produces the defining ocular motility deficit.
Malignancy originates in testosterone-producing Leydig cells, the endocrine component of the testis; metastatic sites are not assigned.
Pathological sclerosis and hardening of skin; the record does not establish systemic sclerosis or an autoimmune mechanism.
Lysosomal storage disorders; skeletal malformations and neurodevelopmental impairment are major group features, each affecting a substantial share; severity varies by subtype.
Inflammation of the biceps tendon sheath; this usually mechanical disorder does not establish an autoimmune or infectious mechanism.
Juvenile CLN2 is a neurodegenerative lysosomal storage disease; retinal degeneration varies in atypical CLN2, with insufficient evidence here for the 30% threshold.
Unilateral congenital duplication and fusion of digits; ancestry identifies a nonsyndromic skeletal malformation.
Marrow failure defines disease; biliary atresia, esophageal atresia and absent thumb each occur in 1/2 reported patients; ASD (1/2) omitted at cap; very small sample.
Mitochondrial myopathy; encephalopathy and seizures are reported in 30-79%; respiratory failure reflects respiratory muscle weakness rather than direct lung damage.
Disease of the nail; infectious and neoplastic subtypes do not define the entire umbrella.
Papilloma originates in respiratory mucosa of the ethmoid sinus; proximity to bone and the eye does not establish their involvement.
Diffuse rigid, thickened skin defines disease; respiratory insufficiency in 30-79% results from restricted chest movement, without established direct lung injury.
Lethal osteosclerotic skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia, pulmonic stenosis and pathological skin thickening are each reported in 30-79%.
Chronic suppurative bacterial infection predominantly damages skin and subcutis; visceral infection is a minority presentation.
Renal tubular sodium transport disorder defined by hypertension and hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis; each is documented in both reported patients.
Defined by benign neoplastic origin in an endocrine organ, whether functioning or nonfunctioning; heterogeneous child locations do not define the umbrella.
Branched-chain amino acid metabolism defect; toxic encephalopathy is a defining, near-universal untreated manifestation; central respiratory failure does not imply lung injury.
Aortic aneurysm/dissection defines disease; dural ectasia (3/4) need not damage nerves, and arachnodactyly (2/6) alone does not establish skeletal damage.
